key_facts: Tier-one N-type solar panels sold for {{data.solar_prices.panel_rs_per_w.low|rs2}} to {{data.solar_prices.panel_rs_per_w.high|rs2}} per watt in Pakistan in the dealer price lists and news reports Wattlyst checked on {{data.solar_prices._meta.checked}}; the full spread seen across sources was {{data.solar_prices.panel_rs_per_w.min_low_seen|rs2}} to {{data.solar_prices.panel_rs_per_w.max_high_seen|rs2}} per watt.

A solar panel's price = its watts × the rupees per watt: a {{in.panel_w|int}} W panel is about {{out.panel_low_rs|rs}} to {{out.panel_high_rs|rs}}, a {{ex.3.in.panel_w|int}} W panel about {{ex.3.out.panel_low_rs|rs}} to {{ex.3.out.panel_high_rs|rs}}.

Panels are sold in Pakistan by the watt, not by the piece: a bigger panel costs more, but the rupees per watt of tier-one brands such as LONGi, Jinko, JA Solar, Trina and Canadian Solar sit in the same narrow band.
Panels alone are a minority of an installed system's price; the inverter, structure, cabling, protection and labour make up the rest (see the solar system price page).
These are secondary-source retail ranges (dealer lists, price guides and news), not an official rate; they move with the rupee, import costs and tax and are refreshed monthly.

formula.text: Price per panel = panel W × Rs per W; price of all panels = price per panel × number of panels (low and high end of the typical range)
lines: Rs per W = typical retail panel-only rate from Wattlyst price data (median of the sources' low and high figures)
kW of panels = panel W × panels ÷ 1000
excludes inverter, structure, cables, protection, labour and delivery

sections.h2: Solar panel price per watt in Pakistan
p: The typical retail price of a tier-one N-type solar panel is {{out.rs_per_w_low|rs2}} to {{out.rs_per_w_high|rs2}} per watt, the median of the low and high figures in the sources listed under Sources (checked {{data.solar_prices._meta.checked}}). Individual quotes ranged from {{data.solar_prices.panel_rs_per_w.min_low_seen|rs2}} to {{data.solar_prices.panel_rs_per_w.max_high_seen|rs2}} per watt, with the top of that spread for premium bifacial stock.

Dealers in Pakistan price panels by the watt, which is why a quote often reads as a per-watt figure rather than a price per plate. Multiply the per-watt rate by the panel's rated watts to get the price of one panel; the calculator above does that for any size and quantity.

A {{in.panel_w|int}} W panel, a common size in the dealer price lists, costs about {{out.panel_low_rs|rs}} to {{out.panel_high_rs|rs}} at the typical rate. {{in.panels|int}} of them give {{out.kw|2}} kW of panels for {{out.total_low_rs|rs}} to {{out.total_high_rs|rs}}, which is roughly the panel bill of a five-kilowatt home system.

Larger panels such as {{ex.3.in.panel_w|int}} W cost more each, about {{ex.3.out.panel_low_rs|rs}} to {{ex.3.out.panel_high_rs|rs}}, but you need fewer of them and fewer clamps and rails. Check that the roof, the structure and the inverter's input voltage suit the larger size before choosing it.

sections.h2: Solar panel rate today by brand: LONGi, Jinko, Canadian Solar and others
p: The sources behind our range quote LONGi, Jinko, JA Solar, Trina and Canadian Solar N-type panels, and they disagree with each other about which brand is cheapest in a given week. Wattlyst does not publish a price per brand because no source updates brand prices reliably; the per-watt range above covers the tier-one brands the sources list.

Within a brand, the newest panel lines (higher efficiency, bifacial glass) carry a premium over older stock. Ask the dealer for the exact model, the warranty and whether the stock is documented (imported with full duty paid), then compare the per-watt rate with the range above.

sections.h2: N-type solar panel price vs older panels
p: Most panels in our sources' lists are N-type (TOPCon or similar), which lose a little less output in heat and over the years than the older P-type panels. One of our sources, PhoneWorld, lists premium N-type bifacial panels above regular A-grade stock, and another, PriceData, lists smaller tier-two panels well below the tier-one range.

A cheaper panel is only a saving if its warranty, its real output and the seller can be trusted. Lower per-watt prices from unknown brands or undocumented stock are common; use the tier-one range as the benchmark.

sections.h2: Solar plate price in Lahore, Karachi and other cities
p: Our sources quote national prices; one news report covers the Karachi market. We have no separate city price list, so the same per-watt range applies as a benchmark in Lahore, Islamabad or Multan. Local prices differ with transport, stock and the dealer's margin; ask two or three dealers for a per-watt figure on the same model.
Then move from panels to the whole system: the solar system price page and the quote checker show what a complete installed system typically costs.

mistakes: Comparing a per-panel price with a per-watt price. Convert every quote to rupees per watt (price ÷ panel watts) before comparing.
Treating the panel price as the system price. Panels are only part of an installed system; the inverter, structure, cables, protection and labour come on top.
Chasing the lowest per-watt rate without checking the brand, model, warranty and stock. Undocumented or unknown-brand panels are often cheaper for a reason.
Buying panels before sizing the system. Size the array from your bill and roof first; then the number of panels decides the price.
safety: Solar panels in series produce DC voltage that can kill and cannot be switched off while the sun shines; have a licensed electrician or registered installer mount, wire and earth them, with DC breakers and surge protection in the quote.

faq.q: What is the solar panel price in Pakistan today?
faq.a: About {{out.rs_per_w_low|rs2}} to {{out.rs_per_w_high|rs2}} per watt for tier-one N-type panels in the sources we checked on {{data.solar_prices._meta.checked}}, so a {{in.panel_w|int}} W panel costs about {{out.panel_low_rs|rs}} to {{out.panel_high_rs|rs}}. Prices change monthly.

faq.q: What is the price of a {{in.panel_w|int}} W solar panel?
faq.a: About {{out.panel_low_rs|rs}} to {{out.panel_high_rs|rs}} at the typical rate of {{out.rs_per_w_low|rs2}} to {{out.rs_per_w_high|rs2}} per watt. The exact price depends on brand, model and dealer.

faq.q: What is the solar panel price per watt in Pakistan?
faq.a: {{out.rs_per_w_low|rs2}} to {{out.rs_per_w_high|rs2}} per watt is the typical range for tier-one panels, with individual quotes from {{data.solar_prices.panel_rs_per_w.min_low_seen|rs2}} to {{data.solar_prices.panel_rs_per_w.max_high_seen|rs2}}. These are secondary-source retail figures, not an official rate.

faq.q: What is the price of LONGi, Jinko or Canadian Solar panels?
faq.a: Our sources quote these brands inside the tier-one range of {{out.rs_per_w_low|rs2}} to {{out.rs_per_w_high|rs2}} per watt, and they disagree on which is cheapest. We do not publish brand prices; ask dealers for a per-watt quote on the exact model and compare it with this range.

faq.q: How much do panels for a five-kilowatt system cost?
faq.a: {{ex.1.in.panels|int}} panels of {{ex.1.in.panel_w|int}} W ({{ex.1.out.kw|2}} kW) cost about {{ex.1.out.total_low_rs|rs}} to {{ex.1.out.total_high_rs|rs}}, panels only. The full installed system costs more; see the solar system price page.

faq.q: Why do solar panel prices change so often?
faq.a: Panels are imported, so their price moves with the dollar rate, international panel prices, duties and sales tax. Wattlyst refreshes this range monthly and prints the date it was checked.
